manifest_row.title: New data platform illuminates history of humans' environmental impact

screening.main_topic: ZooArchNet, a digital platform connecting zooarchaeological and biodiversity records to study the history of human-animal interactions and environmental change.
screening.climate_relevance: The article discusses how people responded to past climate change, including changing diets as the climate cooled and challenges such as rising sea levels and fluctuating temperatures. It presents historical records as useful for understanding present-day climate responses, but climate change is one aspect of the broader environmental and archaeological subject.
screening.reason: The article is mainly about a research data platform and long-term human impacts on animals and landscapes. Its discussion of past climate change and human responses is meaningful but not central enough for CORE.
